headline: Highest risk is TREK’s real-time collaborative MCP/browser surface; pairwise interaction with dbt-core is otherwise mostly limited to allowlisted egress and shared data handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core has no documented inbound shared channel, while TREK exposes MCP and browser-driven collaboration. A prompt-injection path is therefore not default between them; it would require an unusual bridge such as manual copy-paste or an external shared workspace. The blast radius is limited because dbt-core is not shown ingesting TREK output automatically.
conditions: IF an operator copies TREK-generated text into dbt-core prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is added between the agents, TREK content can steer dbt-core.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted TREK output into dbt-core runs.
Add a human review step before any dbt model or macro changes.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: isolate MCP tools from dbt execution contexts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress; TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets, and also uses files plus MCP. If they share a workspace or operator account, sensitive TREK data can flow into dbt-core outputs or logs. The interaction is inferred, but both profiles show enough surface to make leakage plausible in default collaborative use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or database, TREK secrets can be exposed to dbt-core artifacts.
IF TREK logs or uploads are imported into dbt workflows, sensitive travel data can leak into downstream outputs.
mitigations: Separate storage for dbt and TREK artifacts.
Rotate any secrets that may have been placed in TREK uploads or logs.
Restrict dbt runs to non-sensitive schemas.
Review allowlisted egress destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls and redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core writes to a data warehouse, and TREK is a collaborative app with files, WebSocket, OIDC, and MCP surfaces plus multiple instances. Even without explicit filesystem write claims for dbt-core, both agents can mutate shared backend resources if deployed together. Uncertainty about exact write scopes pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same warehouse, database, or shared API credentials, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF TREK and dbt-core are run under one orchestrator without locking, state races can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent.
Use distinct databases or schemas.
Add locking around shared mutable resources.
Schedule dbt and TREK write windows separately.
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is described as a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by operators or downstream automation. dbt-core can then transform or publish those outputs without an explicit verification step. The pairwise pathway exists, but there is no direct evidence of automatic action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF TREK-generated itineraries or facts are fed into dbt models without validation, errors can propagate.
IF dbt outputs are used as source-of-truth reports for TREK workflows, incorrect data can cascade.
mitigations: Require source validation before dbt ingestion.
Mark TREK outputs as untrusted by default.
Add checksum or schema checks on imported records.
Have a human approve any downstream publication.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, documents, photos, and country visit history, while dbt-core touches warehouse data and can egress to allowlisted endpoints. If regulated or residency-bound travel data is processed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. dbt-core has no matching compliance claims, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF EU personal data or travel documents are routed through dbt-core, residency or retention controls may be violated.
IF TREK secrets are logged into dbt artifacts, subject-rights and retention handling can fail.
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it to either agent.
Exclude secrets and documents from dbt inputs.
Set retention limits on TREK logs and uploads.
Confirm hosting region for any shared backend.
requires-engineering: document DPA, residency, and deletion workflows.
